title: Sajid Dynasty
capsule: The Sajid dynasty (ساجیان) was a Muslim Iranian-origin dynasty that governed Azerbaijan and parts of Armenia as vassals of the Abbasid caliphate from 889/890 to 929. Founded by Muhammad ibn Abi'l-Saj, who received Azerbaijan as his governorship, the dynasty produced capable military commanders who suppressed the Kharijite revolt of Hamdan Qarmat and maintained Abbasid authority on the volatile Caucasian frontier. The last Sajid ruler, Yusuf ibn Abi'l-Saj, was defeated and captured by the Abbasid army in 929 after rebelling against the caliph, ending the dynasty's independent power.

The dynasty's core territory in Azerbaijan is well documented in Arabic chronicles; the northern limits of Sajid control in Armenia are less precisely defined.
